To: rhonda@lindenpikediner.example
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Christmas breakfast

Hi Rhonda,

It’s Gary from the bus garage. I’m getting started on our Christmas breakfast again and wanted to see if you have the back room open Saturday, December 19 at 7am. If that date doesn’t work, would Saturday the 12th be available instead? Same time and room either way.

Dwayne sent me the list, and we’re at 24 people, counting Earl and Carol. Would the family-style breakfast still be eggs, home fries and biscuits and gravy? Patsy can’t do eggs, so could you let me know what else she might be able to have? Oatmeal, pancakes or whatever you have that would work for her would be great. Everybody else can order their meat off the menu like last year, and separate checks worked fine, so let’s do that again.

Lonnie is using a walker since his hip, so we’ll need to use the side door with no steps. Could you let me know if that door will be open for us, or if there’s anything we need to do when we get there?

Also, last year the coffee ran out around 8:15 when the urn quit. I know you felt bad about it, and I appreciate you saying you’d have a backup next time. Would you be able to have a backup coffee pot ready this year, just in case? We all count on that coffee early in the morning.

You mentioned $11 a head last year. That seemed fair, and we’re fine if it’s gone up a little, so just let me know what the price is now.

One other thing, and please keep this quiet from Earl: his last day driving is the 18th, after 31 years, so we’d like to do something small for him at breakfast. He loves your cinnamon rolls, and honestly they’re better than any cake. Would you rather we bring a cake from Sugarcreek, or could we do a big tray of your cinnamon rolls with a candle? We don’t want to make a big production of it, just something nice that the guys can do for him.

I’ll get you the final count by the Wednesday before, like you asked last year. Thanks for helping us make this a good morning for everybody, and for putting up with our crew every Christmas.

Thanks,
Gary
